question: Whether RPC over TCP is recorded as RPC over ALPC is - each call paired with its stop, carrying no byte - its bytes on the TCP connection beneath it and nowhere else, and what a capture holds of it at the server's end and of its other end.
answer: As over ALPC at the client's end, and not at the server's. Each truth call was one client call to the endpoint mapper's map procedure, its start naming protocol 1 where FX-RPC-001's local calls name 3, paired with its stop by activity id and carrying no byte; beneath them each client held one TCP connection to the endpoint mapper's host on port 135, whose sends and receives - a call's request and answer each, and one bind - held every byte, alike at both ends, so nothing was counted twice. No ALPC message carried any call, so under RPC peers none found its other end, each for no send on its thread. And the endpoint mapper's records of the calls it served over TCP carried no activity id, so its starts and stops each paired with nothing: a call served over TCP read as two unpaired records, each start followed on its thread by its stop. Five runs found it so, nothing lost.

capture.command: icat record --profile explore|rpc-peers --duration 20, machine-wide, beside InterCat.TestWorkloads rpc-tcp --calls 64 --delay 40, or --calls 256 --concurrency 8 --delay 0, --start-after 6; then icat operations --pid <client> and --pid <the endpoint mapper's host> --calls 10000, icat processes, and icat evidence of the two processes' RPC and TCP records

runs.run: Explore, eight clients at once, 256 calls
Explore, eight clients at once, 256 calls: the run the ledgers hold
Explore, one client, 64 calls 40 ms apart
RPC peers, eight clients at once, 256 calls
RPC peers, one client, 64 calls 40 ms apart

ledger: fixtures/FX-RPC-002/evidence/calls.csv and transport.csv, of the run the ledgers hold: each call record of the client, and of the endpoint mapper's host its starts of the endpoint mapper's interface in the client's window and every stop there that carried no activity id - its 100 ns reading after the first, side, start or stop, process, thread, a number standing for its activity id (0 for none), interface, procedure, protocol and status - and each TCP record of the client's connections to port 135, at both ends, with its kind, bytes, ports and thread. A test reads them as a session's records and derives its calls, relationships and bytes.
note: The server's records name no client, so a local call another process made to the endpoint mapper in the client's window is counted beside the runs, never in the ledgers. The calls carry no credentials and the endpoint mapper asked for none.
